subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should native `openclaw backup create` gain user-controlled exclude patterns now, and if so should the permanent shape be the broader policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower flag-only version?
rationale: The feature adds CLI surface and backup selection policy that can protect secrets but can also make archives unrestorable if defaults or protected-path handling are wrong.

options.title: Review PR 44288 as the candidate
options.body: Use the existing PR as the product/security discussion point, requiring conflict resolution, real backup proof, and explicit decisions on defaults and protected paths before merge.

options.title: Narrow to explicit excludes only
options.body: Ask for a smaller implementation that adds repeatable `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` without smart defaults or automatic ignore-file discovery.

options.title: Defer native controls
options.body: Keep native backup coarse and point users to external backup tooling such as the linked Keep My Claw workaround until maintainers sponsor core semantics.

recommendation.title: Review PR 44288 as the candidate
recommendation.body: Use the existing PR as the product/security discussion point, requiring conflict resolution, real backup proof, and explicit decisions on defaults and protected paths before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The backup CLI was introduced in the history under this author, making them the strongest routing candidate for native command semantics.
